item.title: NBC launches application on Google Play
item.description: Former NBC Information Technology Manager, Luan Bole explaining more on the application’s services. (NBC News) The State Broadcaster's news and information can be easily accessed anywhere in the world.
item.content:encoded:
Former NBC Information Technology Manager, Luan Bole explaining more on the application’s services. (NBC News)

The State Broadcaster's news and information can be easily accessed anywhere in the world.

This is following the launch of the NBC app on Google Play on Friday.

The National Broadcasting Corporation's services especially news and information from its headquarters to the provincial station will soon be full accessed anywhere in the world, online.

The organization launched the phase one of the NBC app where its television and radio services are now available on.

Former NBC Information Technology Manager, Luan Bole who was at the forefront of this initiative.

Ms Bole attributed this milestone to the efforts of the Managing Director Kora Nou and the past board to set up the app given the rapidly changing media landscape and digital advancements.

She also stated that the app it also a good tool for the organization to generate revenue from.

The milestone is testament to the State Broadcaster's efforts to improve its services and reach to the people of Papua New Guinea and the rest of the world.

item.title: NBC’s new board members sworn in
item.description: Henao Iduhu the former Deputy Chairman of the NBC board has now been elevated to Chairman post (NBC News) The National Broadcasting Corporation new board members were sworn in yesterday, following the end of the last board's term.
item.content:encoded:
Henao Iduhu the former Deputy Chairman of the NBC board has now been elevated to Chairman post (NBC News)

The National Broadcasting Corporation new board members were sworn in yesterday, following the end of the last board's term.

The new board members are Henao Iduhu as Chairman, Deputy Chairman Chris Mora and directors Esther Igo, Peter Mokai and newly appointed board director Hulala Tokome.

When congratulating them on their appointments, NBC Managing Director Kora Nou expressed that their leadership comes at an important time in the state broadcaster's history to navigate through the challenges and opportunities ahead.

Mr Iduhu assured the management and staff of the NBC that they will continue to progress the work of the last board.

The former board's term expired in June this year.

Information and Communications Technology Minister Robert Naguri says he is pleased that the appointment of the new NBC board is achieved within a short space of time since his appointment as the minister responsible for ICT

The minister is confident in the new board to progress the work of the last board as well as progress and perform in the next three years

item.title: National Okuk Highway blocked at Erap following PMV attack
item.description: The highway remains blocked as police work to restore peace and allow traffic to resume (Supplied) The National Okuk Highway at Erap in Morobe Province is currently blocked as police work to prevent a possible confrontation between armed men from Markham and settlers at Ngsuampun.
item.content:encoded:
The highway remains blocked as police work to restore peace and allow traffic to resume (Supplied)

The National Okuk Highway at Erap in Morobe Province is currently blocked as police work to prevent a possible confrontation between armed men from Markham and settlers at Ngsuampun.

The situation follows an alleged attack on a Markham PMV bus yesterday, during which the bus crew was reportedly assaulted, with one crew member said to be receiving hospital treatment.

Following the incident, frustrated men from Markham travelled in truckloads towards Ngsuampun but were stopped at Erap by Morobe Provincial Police Commander, Acting Chief Superintendent Robert Baim, before they could proceed further.

PPC Baim addressed the men and warned them not to proceed to Ngsuampun or take the law into their own hands.

He also warned the Ngsuampun community that the suspects allegedly involved in the attack must be handed over to police before 4:06pm today.

The suspects have not yet been arrested, and police are negotiating with both factions to calm tensions and prevent possible violence.

The highway remains blocked as police work to restore peace and allow traffic to resume.

Markham leaders told police this was the fifth reported incident involving their PMV buses being held up along the highway, saying repeated attacks had caused growing frustration among PMV operators and the community.

Police efforts are continuing to prevent the situation from escalating.

item.title: PM Marape departs for Timor-Leste independence celebrations ahead of PNG investment conference in Sydney
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape departs for Timor-Leste this morning to attend celebrations marking the 51st anniversary of the country’s Proclamation of Independence, before travelling to Sydney, Australia, to open the Papua New Guinea Investment Week Conference. PM Marape said his visit to Timor-Leste was in reciprocation of President José Manuel Ramos-Horta’s attendance at Papua New Guinea’s 50th I
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister James Marape departs for Timor-Leste this morning to attend celebrations marking the 51st anniversary of the country’s Proclamation of Independence, before travelling to Sydney, Australia, to open the Papua New Guinea Investment Week Conference.

PM Marape said his visit to Timor-Leste was in reciprocation of President José Manuel Ramos-Horta’s attendance at Papua New Guinea’s 50th Independence Anniversary celebrations in September 2025.

He said Timor-Leste was a Southeast Asian country with Melanesian cultural affinities and that the visit would further strengthen friendship and bilateral relations between the two countries.

Foreign Affairs Minister, Justin Tkatchenko will represent the Prime Minister at some official engagements on Saturday as the Prime Minister observes the Sabbath.

Mr Marape will then travel to Sydney on Sunday to officially open the Papua New Guinea Investment Week Conference before returning home.

In his absence, Deputy Prime Minister, John Rosso will serve as Acting Prime Minister.

Meanwhile, Mr Marape has called on all Government MPs to attend Parliament next week for three important national matters.

These include the handing down of the 2027 National Budget on Tuesday, December 1, deliberations on Bougainville on Wednesday, December 2, and the passage of the National Budget on Thursday, December 3.

item.title: Parliament to vote on Wednesday, 2nd December
item.description: The date has been set for the much-anticipated vote that will determine the future of Bougainville. Prime Minister James Marape announced that the vote will take place on Wednesday, 2 December 2026.
item.content:encoded:
The date has been set for the much-anticipated vote that will determine the future of Bougainville.

Prime Minister James Marape announced that the vote will take place on Wednesday, 2 December 2026.

After years of ongoing consultation between the National Government and the Autonomous Region of Bougainville regarding the political aspiration of Bougainville, a vote will now take place.

Prime Minister James Marape announced that the vote will be among key agendas for parliament next week.

Members from now until Wednesday have few days to carefully think about the type of vote they will make.

Speaker of Parliament Job Pomat has issued strong calls for members to use this time, to prepare well on their voting choice and for them to all be present for this historic vote.

The ratification vote will come about after two days of debates and following on from the last sitting.

Under the 2001 Peace Agreement, and PNG Constitution, the 2019 referendum, in which an overwhelming 97,7 percent voted for independence is non- binding , leaving the PNG National Parliament with the final ratification decision.

In order for the vote to be accepted, a three – quarter absolute majority must be reached, which is 89 out of 118 members.

item.title: SiPHA’s trip to Gumine saves lives
item.description: Aerial view of Olegain Health Center in Gumine District (Supplied) A surprise health inspection by the Simbu Provincial Health Authority (SiPHA) turned into a life-saving rescue yesterday after the team saved a pregnant mother who was about to give birth by the roadside in Gumine District of Simbu.
item.content:encoded:
Aerial view of Olegain Health Center in Gumine District (Supplied)

A surprise health inspection by the Simbu Provincial Health Authority (SiPHA) turned into a life-saving rescue yesterday after the team saved a pregnant mother who was about to give birth by the roadside in Gumine District of Simbu.

The mother was found in active labour in the open bush during heavy rain, with no medical assistance and no transport.

The SiPHA team took her on board and rushed her to Gomgale Sub-Health Centre,in Kuman Bomai LLG where she safely delivered her baby.

SiPHA Chief Executive Officer Dr Kassi Ken led the Monitoring and Evaluation team on the trip from Dirima to Olegain Health Centre, a four-hour drive through rain and mud-choked tracks.

The visit was to inspect service delivery at Olegain, a remote facility bordering Kambia in Jiwaka Province and Karimui in Simbu.

Speaking to community members at Olegain, Dr Ken raised concerns over deteriorating road conditions and the theft of the facility's ambulance.

The ambulance, funded by the Gumine District Development Authority (DDA), was stolen and later recovered in Jiwaka Province. Police are investigating. Olegain Health Centre remains without emergency transport.

"Where people live, essential services must follow. Our health personnel cannot be expected to walk for days across rugged terrain just to collect basic medical consumables. When roads fail, healthcare fails and our people suffer." Dr Ken said.

Dr Ken urged community leaders to press their local representatives for immediate road rehabilitation, and said he would escalate the issue to provincial and national authorities.

The warning became real on the return journey, when the team encountered the pregnant mother by the roadside.

SiPHA drivers navigated the flooded, washed-out terrain, completing what is normally a three-hour drive to Gomgale in 40 minutes.

Had the team not been passing through at that time, the mother and her unborn child would have been left stranded without transport.

The incident highlights the daily challenges faced by mothers, patients and health workers in remote Simbu, where poor roads, stolen community assets and geographic isolation turn routine medical needs into a matter of life and death.

item.title: Massat: Ratification not the only way
item.description: Bougainville Vice President Ezekiel Masatt, has reminded Members of the House of Representative that the Ratification process currently underway in the National Parliament is not the only way for Bougainville to secure its independence. The Autonomous Bougainville Government has put forward to the National Government its final position mid this year, that it would transition into Self-Government b
item.content:encoded:
Bougainville Vice President Ezekiel Masatt, has reminded Members of the House of Representative that the Ratification process currently underway in the National Parliament is not the only way for Bougainville to secure its independence.

The Autonomous Bougainville Government has put forward to the National Government its final position mid this year, that it would transition into Self-Government by September 2027 and declare independence by 2030.

Since 2001, Bougainville has progressed the Bougainville Peace Agreement which will now culminate with the Ratification where the National Parliament is expected to endorse the aspirations of the people to be independent, expressed in the 2019 Referendum.

The ABG had since expressed that it prefers attaining independence through the Peace Process, where the choice of the people through the Referendum must be endorsed.

In their consultations, the National Government has recognized Bougainville’s wish, and the parties have jointly agreed on the Melanesian Agreement Framework which will guide the lawful and gradual transition of Bougainville into independence.

However, debate during various sessions of the National Parliament since the Referendum Result, the Joint Consultations Report and the Melanesian Agreement Framework have been tabled, have shown that the National Government might not be able to muster the three-quarters majority vote needed to endorse Bougainville’s independence aspiration.

Addressing a briefing of the House of Representatives by officials from the Department of Independence Mission Implementation during the last sitting, Vice President Ezekiel Masatt reminded Members that the Ratification Process under the Peace Agreement is not the only way to attain independence.

He’s pointed out two other ongoing options of using a Constitution to declare independence and lobbying international support.

Ezekiel Masatt says people must not have high expectations on the Ratification Process, but leaders must continue to work to prepare the region for independence according to the timeline put forward by the Autonomous Bougainville Government.

Mr Massat further stressed that the men, women and children of Bougainville will lead the independence agenda.

item.title: Marape urges Parliament not to rush Bougainville vote
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape says the Bougainville agenda must not be rushed. (Image: National Parliament) There is still mixed reaction on the floor of Parliament as the National Parliament continues its final debate on Bougainville’s independence agenda.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister James Marape says the Bougainville agenda must not be rushed. (Image: National Parliament)

There is still mixed reaction on the floor of Parliament as the National Parliament continues its final debate on Bougainville’s independence agenda.

There is still more debate calling for Bougainville to remain part of Papua New Guinea under a higher autonomy arrangement. Others have argued against recognising the result of the 2019 Referendum entirely, while some have thrown their support behind recognising the aspiration for independence and argued for a vote in support of Bougainville’s independence.

The Bougainville independence agenda is an agenda of the National Government, having been brought forward by Bougainville Affairs Minister Manasseh Makiba.

However, from the debates during the various sessions of Parliament, it has become clear that the Government may not muster the numbers to secure Parliament’s support for the result of the Referendum, the Joint Consultations Report and the Melanesian Framework Agreement, which were tabled in August by Minister Makiba.

Debates over the various sittings have shown that the ratification vote will be taken by Members voting as individuals, based on their personal conscience rather than along party or political lines.

More debate ensued today, with the House adjourning until tomorrow to continue deliberations.

Prime Minister James Marape told the House that there is no need to rush the debate to take the ratification vote.

He says that, with Papua New Guinea’s sovereignty at stake, there is no need to rush Parliament’s consideration of the matter.

Marape is urging every Member to have a say on the issue before the final ratification is decided during this critical sitting of the House.
